The following has been written as a guide, as opposed to a simple tutorial. It is intended to house as much information as possible for reference. Because of this, it may seem overwhelming or complicated for those new to the subject.

For a more straight-forward guide, refer to @Shiny's guide on spriting.

What is a sprite sheet?

A sprite sheet is a single image that holds an array of two or more smaller images. Here is an example, which is one of Voat's very own sprite sheets. Voat uses a different sprite sheet for night mode.

Sprite sheets are used to increase the performance of your web browser by reducing the number of HTTP requests your browser makes; [1] instead of asking Voat for three separate images three times, your browser can ask Voat for three separate images once. Because of this, sprite sheets are typically used for sprites that appear a lot throughout a web page, especially those that appear more than once.

Create a Sprite Sheet

Sprite sheets are created either manually in many image editors/graphics creators or automatically, using a program or web service.

Creating a Sprite Sheet Manually

Tip: For this section, we're going to be using Pinta, a free and open-source, cross-platform, basic image editor.

Starting from a Template

Download the template I made of the sprite sheet and open it up in Pinta.

Each sprite (or icon) is on its own layer so you can edit the sprites on an individual level. You can think of each sprite as a square; a certain-sized square. [A] [B] Squares cannot overlap each other even though the sprites themselves look like they don't. If they overlap even by a pixel, part of one sprite is going to appear in the other.

Here is a reference for the default-sized sprites:

Sprite Dimensions Position Use
Sprite Name w x h px (x, y)  
Mail: Default 18 x 12 px (0, 0) No Messages
Mail: Red 18 x 12 px (18, 0) You have mail!
Settings 16 x 16 px (56, 0) "Manage" settings
Lightbulb 10 x 16 px (86, 0) Toggle night mode
Arrow (normal): Upvote: Default 16 x 16 px (0, 12) 'Front' pages, everywhere on mobile
Arrow (normal): Upvote: Active 16 x 16 px (16, 12) ″
Arrow (normal): Downvote: Default 16 x 16 px (0, 28) ″
Arrow (normal): Downvote: Active 16 x 16 px (16, 28) ″
Arrow (mini): Upvote: Default 12 x 12 px (32, 12) Comments
Arrow (mini): Upvote: Active 12 x 12 px (44, 12) ″
Arrow (mini): Downvote: Default 12 x 12 px (32, 24) ″
Arrow (mini): Downvote: Active 12 x 12 px (44, 24) ″
Expando (normal): Default: Default 16 x 16 px (0, 44) 'Front' pages
Expando (normal): Default: Hover 16 x 16 px (16, 44) ″
Expando (normal): Active: Default 16 x 16 px (0, 60) ″
Expando (normal): Active: Hover 16 x 16 px (16, 60) ″
Expando (normal): Busy: Default 16 x 16 px (0, 76) ″
Expando (normal): Busy: Hover 16 x 16 px (16, 76) ″
Expando (big): Default 32 x 32 px (32, 44) 'Front' pages on mobile
Expando (big): Active 32 x 32 px (64, 44) ″
Expando (big): Busy 32 x 32 px (32, 76) ″

Go ahead and create your own sprites and compile them into your sprite sheet. Make sure they match the dimensions and positions in the table!

Saving the Sprite Sheet

First, save the file as a *.ora file so the layers remain intact if you want to come back and make some edits.

When you're done with the sprite sheet and want to publish it to be used on your subverse, save the file as a *.png file and upload it to an image hosting service, such as Imgur or Pomf.se. Take note the direct image URL (which should end in .png). We'll use it later.

Apply the Sprite Sheet with CSS

Now that the sprite sheet is ready to be used, we need to apply it to your subverse using a cascading style sheet (CSS). We'll start with the cookie-cutter code template:

/* mail */
#mail.havemail,
#mail.nohavemail {
 background: url( SPRITE_SHEET_URL );
 width: 18px;
 height: 12px;
}
 #mail.havemail { background-position: -18px 0; }
 #mail.nohavemail { background-position: 0 0; }

/* toggle night mode */
#nightmodetoggle {
 background: url( SPRITE_SHEET_URL );
 background-position: -86px 0;
 width: 10px;
 height: 16px;
}

/* voting arrows */
.arrow-upvote,
.arrow-upvoted,
.arrow-downvote,
.arrow-downvoted {
 background: url( SPRITE_SHEET_URL );
 width: 16px;
 height: 16px;
}
 .arrow-upvote { background-position: 0 -12px; }
 .arrow-upvoted { background-position: -16px -12px; }
 .arrow-downvote { background-position: 0 -28px; }
 .arrow-downvoted { background-position: -16px -28px; }

.comment .arrow-upvote,
.comment .arrow-upvoted,
.comment .arrow-downvote,
.comment .arrow-downvoted {
 background: url( SPRITE_SHEET_URL );
 width: 12px;
 height: 12px;
}
 .comment .arrow-upvote { background-position: -32px -12px; }
 .comment .arrow-upvoted { background-position: -44px -12px; }
 .comment .arrow-downvote { background-position: -32px -24px; }
 .comment .arrow-downvoted { background-position: -44px -24px; }

/* mobile voting arrows */
\@media ( max-width: 700px ) {
 .comment .arrow-upvote,
 .comment .arrow-upvoted,
 .comment .arrow-downvote,
 .comment .arrow-downvoted {
 background: url( SPRITE_SHEET_URL );
 width: 16px;
 height: 16px;
 }
 .comment .arrow-upvote { background-position: 0 -12px; }
 .comment .arrow-upvoted { background-position: -16px -12px; }
 .comment .arrow-downvote { background-position: 0 -28px; }
 .comment .arrow-downvoted { background-position: -16px -28px; }
}

/* expandos */
.expando-button.selftext.collapsed,
.expando-button.selftext.expanded,
.expando-button.selftext.loading {
 background: url( SPRITE_SHEET_URL );
 width: 16px;
 height: 16px;
}
 .expando-button.selftext.collapsed { background-position: 0 -44px;}
 .expando-button.selftext.collapsed:hover { background-position: -16px -44px;}
 .expando-button.selftext.expanded { background-position: 0 -60px;}
 .expando-button.selftext.expanded:hover { background-position: -16px -60px;}
 .expando-button.selftext.loading { background-position: 0 -76px;}
 .expando-button.selftext.loading:hover { background-position: -16px -76px;}

/* mobile expandos */
\@media ( max-width: 700px ) {
 .expando-button.selftext.collapsed,
 .expando-button.selftext.expanded,
 .expando-button.selftext.loading {
 background: url( SPRITE_SHEET_URL );
 width: 32px;
 height: 32px;
 }
 .expando-button.selftext.collapsed,
 .expando-button.selftext.collapsed:hover { background-position: -32px -44px;}
 .expando-button.selftext.expanded,
 .expando-button.selftext.expanded:hover { background-position: -64px -44px;}
 .expando-button.selftext.loading,
 .expando-button.selftext.loading:hover { background-position: -32px -76px;}
}

Warning: Due to a bug with how Voat parses @, delete the backslash \ before the at symbol @ before media.

Replace SPRITE_SHEET_URL with the direct URL to your sprite sheet.

You'll find the table in the previous section useful here. Each sprite has a height and width and a position (background-position), x and y.

Note: Because of the way CSS parses background-position, all nonzero numbers need to be negative (unless you want to deal in the inverse).

The code here shouldn't be changed besides adding your sprite sheet URL unless you've changed the positioning and/or sizes of the sprites.

Recap

  • A sprite sheet is just a bunch of images inside one image, used to boost how quickly a website loads.
  • You can create your own sprite sheet using a simple image editor or a web service online.
  • The code is almost entirely copy-paste. The average joe should only ever change SPRITE_SHEET_URL with the URL of the sprite sheet uploaded online. Also, make sure to delete the \ before the @! And make sure those background-position numbers stay negative.

That's it! If you've followed along well enough, you should have been able to change the sprites. If you have any questions or concerns about this guide, go ahead and ask below. :-)
